newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee down on dlr rise, currency shortage.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee down on dlr rise, currency shortage.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against the dollar and pound on Tuesday on international trends and hard currency shortage in banks, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.3360 against the dollar from 20.2995 on Monday. Against the pound, the rupee weakened to a mean of 31.7420 from 31.6825 on Monday.
Dealers said a hard currency shortage in commercial banks and the dollar's overnight strengthening in international markets was behind the weaker rupee at Tuesday's fixing.
"We are hoping the central bank will intervene in the interbank market today to relieve the shortage situation," one dealer said.
The central bank was last reported selling dollars in the interbank forex market eight days ago.
Dealers attributed banks' hard currency shortages to an undersupply of the country's export earnings directly in the local commercial banking circuit.
"Net earnings from the textiles sector may satisfy banks to around 30 percent of their customers' requirements while proceeds from the tourism sector for far much less," one said.
Three quarters of sugar exports, the country's largest hard currency earner, is kept by the central bank and is sold to commercial banks through interventions.
Dealers said such interventions are insufficient to meet all their customers' demand requirements.
The remaining quarter is put on tender sale directly to banks by the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate.
But the Syndicate tenders were also reported as failing to eradicate the shortage situation in commercial banks. The Syndicate last held its sale tender on Wednesday.
